name: create_collection
title: Create a collection
description: Make a named collection to index documents into; it records the embedding model and dimension the server uses now, and only that model can search or grow it later. Creating one that exists with the same description is a no-op. The first collection also creates the tables. embedding_provider says where its chunks are embedded when indexed: local (the server's own embed endpoint, the default) or a remote service running the same model, which is faster for a large corpus and sends the documents' text there. A remote provider is accepted only after it embeds probe texts as the local endpoint does (cosine at least 0.999), since every question is embedded locally. Naming another provider for an existing collection moves it there, with the same probe; chunks already embedded stay, as both providers' vectors are alike.

name.description: Lowercase letters, digits, - and _, at most 63 characters.

description.description: What the collection holds, for whoever lists it later.

embedding_provider.description: Where indexing embeds this collection's chunks. Default: local for a new collection, unchanged for an existing one.

name: drop_collection
title: Drop a collection
description: Delete a collection and everything indexed in it (documents, chunks, embeddings). The source files are not touched; indexing them again rebuilds it. Acts outside the computer: the client asks the user to approve each call.

name.description: A collection's name, as list_collections shows it.

name: expand
title: Read around a hit
description: The chunks just before and after a search result in its document, in order, the hit marked: the context a passage needs.

collection.description: A collection's name, as list_collections shows it.

name: health
title: Health
description: Whether search and indexing can work: the database (its vector and unaccent extensions, the tables and their vector dimension, how many collections), the embed endpoint (model, revision, dimension), the rerank endpoint (model), and the text extractors found on PATH (pdftotext, ocrmypdf, tesseract with its languages, pandoc), plus the folders it may index from, and whether each remote embedding provider is configured (read from the settings, without calling it). Run this before concluding the server is broken.

name: index_path
title: Index a file or folder
description: Index one file or every file of a folder (under /srv/rag/inbox) into a collection. Reads pdf, png, jpg, jpeg, tif, tiff, bmp, webp, docx, odt, rtf, epub, html, htm, md, markdown, txt, text, csv; PDF pages without a text layer and images are OCRed in the given language. Text is cut into chunks of about 1200 characters that never cross a page or a heading, each with a stable id and its location; only chunks not stored already are embedded, and a file whose sha256 is unchanged (and was read the same way) is passed over, so running it again only redoes what changed. Links are never followed. One file's failure is reported and the rest go on. Chunks are embedded where the collection says (create_collection's embedding_provider); the reply says how many requests and texts, and for a remote provider the tokens and neurons it reported. Slow when local: about 1-2 chunks of that size per second on a CPU, and OCR a few seconds per page.

collection.description: A collection's name, as list_collections shows it.

path.description: A file or folder under /srv/rag/inbox; a relative path is taken from the first. Links are refused.

recursive.description: Also index the folders inside a folder.

language.description: OCR language as tesseract's codes, e.g. eng, ron, deu. Default: the server's. Give the document's one language: a pair such as ron+eng lets the second strip the first's accents. ron also rewrites the old cedilla ş and ţ as ș and ț.

ocr.description: OCR PDF pages that have no text layer, and images.

force.description: Read and chunk files again even when their sha256 is unchanged (embeddings of unchanged chunks are still kept).

prune.description: For a folder: also remove from the index the sources under it that are no longer there (only its own files when recursive is false).

max_files.description: Files read in this call; unchanged files are passed over without counting, so calling again goes on with the rest.

name: list_collections
title: List collections
description: Every collection with its description, the embedding model it was built with, where its chunks are embedded (provider and that provider's model), what a remote provider has cost it (tokens, neurons), and how many documents and chunks it holds.

name: list_sources
title: List indexed sources
description: The files indexed in a collection: path, sha256, size, kind, pages, chunks and when, in path order, a page at a time.

collection.description: A collection's name, as list_collections shows it.

prefix.description: Only sources whose path starts with this; end a folder with /.

name: read_document
title: Read an indexed document
description: A document's text as indexed, chunk by chunk with each one's location, up to max_chars per call; next_from continues.

collection.description: A collection's name, as list_collections shows it.

source.description: The source path, as search or list_sources shows it.

name: remove_source
title: Remove a source
description: Remove one indexed file, or every indexed file under a folder, from a collection's index. The files themselves are not touched.

collection.description: A collection's name, as list_collections shows it.

path.description: The absolute path as list_sources shows it, or a folder above several. Not / itself: drop_collection removes everything.

name: search
title: Search
description: Find the passages that answer a question, in any language the model reads (a Romanian question finds a Romanian passage worded differently). Hybrid: the nearest chunks by embedding and the full-text matches of any of its words (accents ignored), fused by reciprocal rank; then the reranker reads the best candidates against the question and decides the order. Each result has its collection, chunk id, source path, location (page or heading), text and scores. expand reads around a hit, read_document the whole document. Reranking is the slow part: about 0.5 s per candidate on a CPU.

query.description: The question, in full sentences: the reranker reads it as written.

collections.description: Where to search. Default: every collection.

items.description: A collection's name, as list_collections shows it.

source_prefix.description: Only sources whose path starts with this; end a folder with /.

candidates.description: Fused candidates the reranker reads; more finds more and costs time.

rerank.description: false returns the fused order, without the reranker: fast, less precise.

max_chars.description: Each result's text is cut to about this many characters.
